title: Diversify workload corpus and establish signed golden baselines for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current benchmarking harness does not adequately represent cross-model and cross-workload variability for the runtime's kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduler. Existing suites focus on a few canonical traces which misses edge patterns (burstiness, long-prefill short-decode, long-decode prefills) that drive tail latency regressions and suboptimal kernel routing.

Goal: Ship a reproducible, signed golden-baseline program plus an expanded workload corpus and stochastic perturbation layer so CI perf gates detect regressions that matter to customers. The work couples: (1) workload corpus diversification across model families, sequence lengths, and KV cache hit distributions; (2) a golden baseline signing mechanism and artifact registry; (3) CI perf gate rules tuned to production-shaped metrics; (4) a stochastic jitter/fuzz harness that surfaces racey scheduler/kernelselection instability.

Scope and non-goals: We will extend the benchmark harness and CI checks and provide tooling to promote golden baselines. We will not change low-level kernel implementations in this ticket — those fixes will be follow-ups referenced by the perf outputs.

Key design decisions: 1) Use stratified sampling across four axes: model family (Llama-like, Mistral-like, transformer-xl variants), prefill length bucket (<=64, 65-512, 513-2048, 2049+), decode patterns (single-token-steady, bursty multi-token), and KV cache-hit ratio (0%, 25%, 75%). 2) Capture runtime config with a "golden signature": SHA256 over (input corpus file SHA, runtime-config JSON, seed, compiler-kernel-version). 3) Store signed golden artifacts in the bench-artifacts registry with immutable metadata and human-readable provenance. 4) CI perf gates compare against the nearest-in-time golden signature and allow auto-promote only after canary runs and two maintainer approvals.

Metrics to record (baseline and CI): p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (prefill and decode considered separately), tail-penalty (p99 - p50), tokens/sec, GPU memory high-water mark, host CPU steal, KV cache hit-rate, kernel selection distribution, time-in-kernel per-layer.

Why this is different: Instead of a single canonical baseline we will maintain a small matrix of signed baselines (model-family x traffic-shape) and a stochastic harness that injects temporal jitter and request coalescing to find brittle scheduling behavior that deterministic runs miss.
acceptance_criteria: Expanded workload corpus: at least 24 representative traces covering 3 model families and 4 prefill/decode buckets added to harness
Golden baseline artifact format defined and implemented (signed SHA256 manifest + runtime-config) with registry entry for at least 3 baselines
CI perf gates added: p95 latency regression threshold <=3% and p99 <=5% vs matching golden baseline; throughput drop guard <=7%
Fuzz harness that injects temporal jitter and request batching available and runs as optional CI job
Operational runbook for baseline promotion, re-measure, and rollback documented and linked
Dashboard tile showing kernel-selection heatmap and baseline delta for recent commits

2025-02-24: Prototype corpus generator completed; generates deterministic trace bundles given a seed and bucket mapping. Baseline manifest includes seed and provenance. (PR: github.com/redwood/bench/PR-1422)
2025-02-27: Implemented golden signature derivation and artifact uploader to bench-artifacts s3 with immutability flag. Uploaded first three signed baselines for small/medium/large sequence shapes.

2025-03-03: CI perf gate prototype integrated into merge pipeline; executing harness in ephemeral infra. Initial thresholds intentionally wide for calibration; will tighten after two calibration runs.
